name: Enphase Energy
old_description: Enphase Energy is headquartered in California and known for its microinverter technology for solar panels, as well as energy storage and management systems. Products are used in residential and commercial PV installations.
about:
Enphase Energy was founded in 2006 by Raghu Belur and Martin Fornage in California. The company is now headquartered in Milpitas, California, and operates as a publicly traded corporation (NASDAQ: ENPH).

The company designs and manufactures solar microinverters, battery energy storage systems, and energy management software. As of 2024, Enphase has shipped approximately 89.4 million microinverters and deployed roughly 5.3 million systems across more than 165 countries. Its global workforce numbers about 2,686 employees, and production is carried out at contract manufacturing facilities in South Carolina and Texas.

Enphase serves residential, commercial, and utility-scale solar markets. Its products are installed by a network of over 5,000 installers worldwide and are used by homeowners, businesses, and utility operators seeking distributed energy solutions. The company also provides design, permitting, and monitoring platforms—such as System Planner, Solargraf, and the Enphase App—to support installers and system owners.

Enphase says its microinverter architecture converts sunlight into a safe, reliable, and scalable energy source, with intelligent microinverters compatible with virtually any solar panel. Paired with award-winning battery technology and an monitoring app, the system aims to give users unprecedented data and control over their energy production and consumption, advancing what the company calls a sustainable future for all.

name: Equipment Exchange Co
old_description: Equipment Exchange Company specializes in the sales and marketing of your idle food processing equipment to a number of food industries, from processed meats to packaging and beyond. Our experienced team and vast inventory provide an excellent opportunity for our clients to turn their idle food processing equipment into cash. EEC is a value-added dealer that has been actively working through eeclink.com since 1996.
about:
Equipment Exchange Company operates from Lake City, Pennsylvania, near Erie, and has been active online through eeclink.com since 1996. The company's team brings over 40 years of combined experience in purchasing, refurbishing, and selling industrial food processing machinery, though the firm itself was established in 1996 as a value-added dealer.

The company purchases idle food processing equipment, refurbishes it, and resells it to food manufacturers. Its project scope ranges from single machines to complete facility liquidations, and it conducts both live and web-based simulcast auctions. Inventory categories span bakery, cooking and freezing, food preparation, labeling, material handling, packaging, refrigeration, and support equipment.

Equipment Exchange serves food processing sectors including meat processing, packaging, bakery, and prepared foods. Customers include plants looking to sell surplus assets and buyers seeking refurbished machinery from brands such as FMC Food Tech and Chester Jensen. The dealer markets equipment to processors across the region, leveraging its location equidistant from Pittsburgh, Cleveland, and Buffalo.

The firm positions itself as a value-added dealer that helps clients convert idle assets into cash through an experienced team and a large inventory. Its long-standing online presence since 1996 and auction capabilities differentiate it in the used equipment market.

about:
Equipment Plus Total Facility Solutions was founded in 1987 by Robbie Taylor in Greenville, North Carolina. The company remains under the leadership of the Taylor family, with Laura Taylor also playing a key role. From its start as a foodservice equipment dealer, it has grown into a total facilities solutions provider for eastern North Carolina.

The firm supplies commercial kitchen equipment, offers equipment rentals, sells smallwares and chemicals, and provides parts, service, and preventive maintenance around the clock. Its 20,000‑square‑foot corporate center houses a showroom, a service dispatch center, a parts inventory valued at more than $250,000, and a custom fabrication shop. A staff of over 30 technicians and salespeople covers a 2,200‑square‑mile service area that includes Greenville, Washington, Wilson, Rocky Mount, New Bern, and surrounding communities.

Customers range from independent restaurants and catering operations to craft breweries and brewpubs. Named clients include Local Oak Brewery, G&K Cafe & Catering, Dickenson Avenue Public House, and Uptown Brewing Company. The company also promotes energy‑efficiency solutions for foodservice facilities.

Equipment Plus distinguishes itself with a “one‑stop‑shop” model that combines sales, installation, service, and project management under one roof, and it emphasizes a ministry‑first culture that directs community outreach and employee wellbeing.

Today the firm provides custom design, fabrication, and installation of metal products across a range of processes. Its shop offers design assist, rolling, HVAC fabrication, laser cutting, press brake forming, welding, and polishing. The company describes itself as one of the Philadelphia area's largest sheet metal firms, though it does not disclose facility size or headcount.

Menold serves clients in architectural, industrial, healthcare, pharmaceutical, utility services, construction, and mechanical contracting sectors. Utility services customers receive a wide variety of fabricated metal parts, and the company works with construction managers and mechanical contractors on project-specific components and systems.

The company emphasizes its eight decades of experience and its ability to mobilize resources for prefabrication, identifying opportunities to streamline field installation. It positions its integrated design-to-installation capability as a differentiator for complex metal systems.

about:
Evans Manufacturing Co. operates from Marysville, Washington, tracing its roots to 1916 when it began as a wire-forming operation. The business changed hands several times before Rod and Mary Long acquired it in 2003, bringing Rod’s production manufacturing experience. In its early years the company ran out of a garage; today it occupies a modern facility equipped with CNC laser cutters, press brakes, and wire-forming machinery.

The shop provides a range of metal fabrication services: laser cutting of sheet metal using a Cincinnati system with an nLight source, CNC bending on press brakes, wire bending on Wafios equipment, MIG/TIG/spot welding of steel, stainless steel, and aluminum, hardware insertion via a Haegar machine, and laser engraving for part marking with an Epilog laser. It produces wire forms such as springs and clips, sheet metal components, and proprietary lines including household items, pet supplies, tech accessories, office supplies, and orchard products.

Customers span agriculture, food production, marine, dairy, medical, and pharmaceutical sectors, as well as military, defense, aerospace, and avionics programs. The company’s wire-forming heritage also serves the commercial fishing industry.

Evans emphasizes treating customer priorities as its own, citing on-time delivery, quality focus, and straightforward communication as differentiators. The ownership team highlights the pain of inflexible suppliers and positions the company as a responsive, quality-driven partner.

name: Excal Inc
old_description: Excal Inc. is a modern brass and bronze foundry serving our customer’s requirements in a variety of ways. We produce sand castings in any volume in a wide range of sizes across any industry with a focus on meeting your quality and delivery needs.
about:
Excal Inc. operates a brass and bronze sand casting foundry in Mills, Wyoming, from an 85,000-square-foot facility that opened in 1991 when founder Fred Harmon relocated the business from its predecessor, Buckeye Brass Foundry (established 1966). The company employs more than 50 people and is now a member of the Foundrion Group, a network of non‑ferrous foundries across North America.

The foundry produces sand castings weighing 1 to 2,000 pounds in a wide range of brass, bronze, and stainless‑steel alloys. Two independent high‑production green‑sand molding lines and two no‑bake/air‑set lines run alongside four melting furnaces capable of 60,000 pounds per day. In‑house capabilities include pattern making, coremaking (with a custom Palmer Coremaker), heat treating, five CNC turning centers, two CNC mills, spectrometer inspection, and an ERP system for full traceability.

Excal serves industries such as pump and valve, water metering, fire protection, electrical, lighting, marine, irrigation, water treatment, and broader waterworks, infrastructure, and energy markets. Customers range from prototype programs to multi‑thousand‑part production runs, all machined to finished condition under one roof.

The company emphasizes built‑in redundancy — multiple molding lines and furnaces prevent single‑point‑of‑failure delays — and full in‑house control from pattern to final inspection. It also highlights flexible volume handling and broad alloy expertise, including the ability to accommodate non‑standard grades on request.

Clients include home builders, commercial contractors, interior designers, and individual homeowners throughout the Boise Valley and beyond — from McCall and Tamarack to Sun Valley, Island Park, and the Treasure Valley cities of Boise, Meridian, Nampa, and Caldwell.

The company emphasizes reliable communication, adherence to budgets, and on-time delivery, building a reputation for consistency among builders who depend on its ability to translate complex designs into finished metalwork.

name: ExoTech Circuits
old_description: Founded in 2022, We specialize in Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) offering contract assembly, integration, and test of high-reliability, mission-critical electronics for the Aerospace and Defense Industry.
about:
ExoTech Circuits was founded in 2022 in Conifer, Colorado. The company is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB/VOSB).

The company provides electronics manufacturing services (EMS) including printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), electronics box assembly and integration, and wire harness and custom cabling. It also offers full functional and environmental testing, material traceability, and documentation for end-item certification (EIDP, CofC). Production takes place in an ISO-7 aerospace-grade cleanroom.

ExoTech serves aerospace and defense customers, supplying space flight hardware such as avionics, power distribution, command and telemetry systems, guidance and navigation units, and ground support equipment. Defense work includes aircraft avionics, communications equipment, electronic warfare systems, and missile fire-control electronics. The company also produces medical and industrial-grade electronics for commercial clients.

The company emphasizes its status as a service-disabled veteran-owned small business and its participation in the Government Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP). Its quality system is compliant with AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015, and it maintains an ISO-7 cleanroom for aerospace-grade processing.

name: Exxelia CalRamic Technologies LLC
old_description: CalRamic Technologies LLC, is a U.S.-based High Voltage Ceramic Capacitor manufacturer with over 30 years’ experience.  Our team focuses on producing exceptional quality capacitors by using superior quality materials with a highly trained team.
about:
Exxelia CalRamic Technologies LLC operates from Reno, Nevada, where it has spent over 30 years manufacturing high-voltage ceramic capacitors. The company was established as a U.S.-based specialist in ceramic capacitor production, focusing on quality materials and a highly trained team.

The product line spans configurations from 500 VDC to 80 KVDC, including MLCC leaded capacitors, high-voltage surface-mount and multilayer chip capacitors, SMPS capacitors, leaded disc capacitors, and custom designs. High-temperature variants rated to 200 °C are also produced. Lean manufacturing principles support rapid prototype turnaround, multiple design derivations, and a range of dielectric options. The company ships in-stock items the same day and serves customers in more than 200 countries.

Capacitors are supplied to defense and commercial aviation, radar systems, geothermal and downhole drilling, flight-control instruments, satellite communications, power generation, and deep-space exploration programs. Additional markets include commercial and industrial equipment, medical devices, commercial aerospace, ground-based military, military aerospace, and high-reliability space satellite systems.

The company emphasizes its 30-plus years of materials engineering expertise, a quality system that exceeds ISO 9001:2015 requirements, and a culture of team-based problem solving. It also maintains an educational library of application notes and training modules to help customers specify the right component.
